_README: House-style rules enforced by validate.py. Example config — replace insurance-specific entries with your own domain's terms. YOU EDIT THIS FILE, not Python. When a reviewer flags a word/phrase that should never recur, add it here and it becomes a publish-blocking FAIL on the next run. Plain JSON: add a line, keep commas valid. ban_swaps + ban_phrases + metaphor_patterns = FAIL (block publish). casual_patterns = FLAG (review). glossary_allow = domain terms that are allowed (glossed, not removed).

ban_swaps.contestability: the time the insurer can dispute a claim

_antiai_README: Pattern families derived from Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing (WP:AISIGNS). copula/superficial-ing/vague-attribution/negative-parallelism/significance-puffery are FAIL (regex via check_patterns in validate.py). knowledge_cutoff + outline_challenges are FLAG. You edit this: add a regex line, keep JSON valid. Em/en dashes and curly quotes are gated as literal characters in validate.py (no list needed).
_proposed_v23_README: PROPOSED WP:AISIGNS families not yet in the enforced set. Wired as the observe-only FLAG check ai_proposed_tells (never blocks publish). Review hits across real runs; a family that proves clean (catches real tells, no false positives) gets promoted: move its lines into a new dedicated key + a FAIL add() in validate.py. Families here: sentence-starting conjunctive adverbs (Additionally/Furthermore/Moreover), editorializing (worth noting / it should be noted), summary closes (in summary / in essence), possessive false-range sweeps (from its X to its Y), chatbot artifacts (great question / I hope this helps / as an AI).
_scene_setter_README: Scene-setter / behavioural openers that violate BLUF — the lede's FIRST sentence must be the answer, not an observation. FAIL if the article's opening sentence matches (canon B1).
_dangling_README: Heading context-words that leave the heading half-baked ('which answer?'). FLAG headings containing these without a concrete noun (canon B2).
_source_allow_README: Example config — replace insurance-specific entries with your own domain's terms. Citations for external stats must come from these authoritative sources only. A non-authoritative publisher = FAIL. Your own first-party data needs no external source. Add the official regulators/government/standards-body substrings your domain trusts.
_product_name_trims_README: Example config — replace insurance-specific entries with your own domain's terms. A HEADING must use the full product name, never a trimmed shorthand. Each {pattern, fix} below = a publish-blocking FAIL when the regex matches a heading. Add the shorthand you keep seeing + the correct full name. Patterns are matched case-insensitively, word-boundaried, on H1/H2/H3 lines only (FAQ questions excluded).
_sales_README: Example config — replace brand-specific entries with your own. Promotional / sell register — FAIL (educate, don't sell). Add new sales tics here, including any that name your brand.
_source_words_README: Example config — replace with your own. Research-mechanism words that must NEVER appear in body prose — FAIL. Add the names of any tools/sources your pipeline uses internally but should never surface in prose.
_glossary_required_README: Example config — replace insurance-specific entries with your own domain's terms. Domain terms that MUST carry a plain-English gloss on first body occurrence. Format: term -> the parenthetical gloss to use, e.g. 'API' -> 'a way for two programs to talk to each other'. validate.py FAILs the article if any term appears in body prose without a gloss within ~80 chars of its first occurrence.

glossary_required.API: a way for two programs to talk to each other
glossary_required.SLA: a service-level agreement, the uptime the vendor promises

_anchor_scoping_README: Example config — replace insurance-specific entries with your own domain's terms. A contextual link anchor must SELF-SCOPE (read alone as a topical phrase). anchor_scoping_tokens: at least one of these words inside the anchor makes it scoped ('pricing plan'). anchor_proper_terms: proper/product terms that scope themselves. A contextual anchor with neither = publish-blocking FAIL (anchor_self_scoping). Add your domain's scoping words or proper terms here.
_repetition_allow_README: Example config — replace with your own domain nouns. Common topic words that are unavoidable and must NOT be flagged by the word-over-repetition check. Add domain nouns here if the check ever flags an obviously-necessary word. Genuine outliers still surface.
_banned_facts_README: Example config — replace with your own. Factual claims that are no longer true under current rules. Body prose stating these as CURRENT (no historical qualifier within ~10 words: was/were/used to be/previously/earlier/formerly/changed from/reduced from/down from) blocks publish. Add {pattern, fix} entries for stale facts your reviewers keep catching.
